message.content:
**Order filled: BUY 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$9,807.60), against a market of $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to make a modest buy. The business picture is steady-to-improving: total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion and gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% (Services gross margin 73.9%), with operating income up 7.4% to $123.2 billion and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion. Diluted EPS was $6.08. The soft spots are real but familiar: iPhone flat at $201.2 billion, iPad −6%, Wearables/Home/Accessories −7%, Greater China −8% to $67.0 billion, and a 24.1% effective tax rate inflated by the one-time $10.2 billion net State Aid charge. One caveat worth flagging: the filing is internally inconsistent on the bottom line — the statements of operations and the "Highlights" line both show "net income $96,995 million" for 2024, but that is actually FY2023's figure; the cash flow statement, the statement of shareholders' equity, and the arithmetic of $123,485 million pretax less $29,749 million tax all give **$93,736 million**, which is also the only figure consistent with the reported $6.08 diluted EPS (96,995 would imply ~$6.30). I therefore recorded net income at $93,736 million in key_figures rather than the headline number, and sized the position conservatively in light of that discrepancy plus roughly 36–37x trailing diluted EPS. The order respects the mandate in full: AAPL only, buy-side, $9,807.60 is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit (with $50,000 cash on hand and the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched), the $222.90 limit sits about 0.08% above the ask and so is effectively at market, and no funds were withdrawn from the account.
